name: Suzhou Garden vs Park Walking Scenes: Visual Perception
description:
Faithful replication of Li & Huang (2022), "Differences in Visual Attraction between Historical Garden and Urban Park Walking Scenes", Land 11:1766. Participants first view 46 walking-scene photographs (23 from Suzhou's historical gardens, 23 from urban parks), each shown for 10 seconds after a 2-second central fixation cross, in random order and with no task. Then they see every photograph again, in a new random order, and rate it on five dimensions of visual perception: fascination, coherence, complexity, legibility and mystery, each on a seven-point scale from −3 (strongly disagree) to +3 (strongly agree). Gender, age, study level and field are asked first. Analysis as in the paper: Cronbach's alpha, then historical garden vs urban park scenes compared on each dimension (Mann–Whitney U). In the original study (61 students, eye tracker in the lab), historical garden scenes were rated more fascinating, coherent, complex and mysterious, and urban park scenes more legible.

Photographs: the paper's Figure A1 (the 46 stimulus photographs, taken by the authors in spring; article CC BY 4.0). They are cut from that figure, so each is only about 450 × 255 pixels. Used with credit; the template is removed if the authors object.

Differences from the original study: (1) no eye tracking: the viewing phase keeps the paper's timing (2 s fixation cross, 10 s per photograph, random order) but records only the viewing order, so the fixation-time and area-of-interest analyses cannot be reproduced; (2) the paper names the five dimensions but does not print the statement wording; the statements here are our own; (3) the paper's rating was a separate online questionnaire after the lab session; here it follows the viewing phase on the same page; (4) photographs are much smaller than the original 1920 × 1080 display; (5) the field-of-study options add "Other" and the study-level options add "Not a student" to the paper's groups (civil engineering, art, urban planning; undergraduate, postgraduate); an online consent checkbox was added.
